bib.title: SWE-EVO: Benchmarking Coding Agents in Long-Horizon Software Evolution Scenarios

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "SWE-EVO: Benchmarking Coding Agents in Long-Horizon Software Evolution Scenarios", Tue Le*, Minh Vu Thai Pham*, Dung Nguyen Manh, Huy Nhat Phan, Nghi D. Q. Bui. Preprint: no venue is printed, only "arXiv:2512.18470v6 [cs.SE] 22 May 2026" and a header date "2026-5-25". First-author affiliation as printed (both equal-contribution first authors): "FPT Software AI Center, Ha Noi, Viet Nam". Others: University of Melbourne; VinUniversity.

COVERAGE: 30 of 30 pages, 76,980 of 76,980 chars. References (pp. 12-17) skimmed. Pages 24-30 are two example problem statements. The captions script returned nothing, so figure captions come from the text extraction; plot values in Figures 5 and 8 are not readable.

CLAIMS

- claim: The benchmark is 48 release-to-release tasks from 7 Python repos; the problem statement is the release-note delta between a tagged version and the next tag, and the gold patch averages 21 files against about 874 tests.
  number: 48 tasks; 7 repos; 20.9 files edited mean (max 105); 610.5 lines edited; 51.0 functions; 81.4 FAIL_TO_PASS mean; 874.0 total tests mean; 2390.5-word spec mean
  setup: Seeded from SWE-bench and SWE-gym instances whose base commit is exactly a version tag; execution-filtered, then manually cut from "a few hundred" candidates. Repo split: dvc 26, dask 8, requests 4, modin 3, pydantic 3, conan 2, scikit-learn 2.
  quote: "SWE-EVOcomprises 48 release-sized tasks requiring multi-step modifications spanning an average of 21 files, validated against test suites averaging 874 tests per instance"
  where: p.1; Table 1 and Figure 3, p.5

- claim: Fix Rate is the fraction of FAIL_TO_PASS tests passing, but is set to 0 for the instance if any PASS_TO_PASS test fails; it is averaged over instances and equals 1 exactly when the instance is resolved.
  number: none
  setup: Definition, Equation 1. Resolved Rate is the SWE-bench binary (all F2P and P2P pass). Patch Apply Rate is also reported.
  quote: "Fix Rate also enforces a regression constraint: if anyPASS_TO_PASS test fails after applying the patch, the instance receives a score of0. This rewards partial fixes while penalizing regressions."
  where: p.7

- claim: The best model resolves 25% and gpt-5.2 falls from 72.80% on SWE-bench Verified to 22.92% here.
  number: 25.00%; 72.80% to 22.92%
  setup: Release note plus linked PR/issue text, internet blocked, OpenHands CodeActAgent (max 100 iterations) and SWE-agent (max 100 LLM calls), medium reasoning effort. The 22.92 is SWE-agent; gpt-5.2 on OpenHands is 18.75. The Verified column is the "bash only" leaderboard figure from swebench.com, a different scaffold and not rerun by the authors. Other matched rows (SWE-agent vs Verified): gpt-5 20.83 vs 65.00; gpt-5-mini 10.42 vs 59.80; o3 6.25 vs 58.40; deepseek-v3p2 23.40 vs 70.00; kimi-k2p5 25.00 vs 70.80.
  quote: "Even the strongest model gpt-5.4 resolves only around25%ofSWE-EVOinstances, and matched-model comparisons show the same pattern:gpt-5.2 drops from 72.80% on SWE-bench Verified to 22.92% onSWE-"
  where: p.8, Table 2

- claim: The top single cell in the tables is not gpt-5.4: glm-4p7 scores 39.58 and glm-5 37.50 on SWE-agent, against 4.17 and 8.33 on OpenHands.
  number: 39.58 / 37.50 vs 4.17 / 8.33
  setup: Same conditions; the authors call it scaffold sensitivity. It contradicts the "best model reaches only 25%" wording.
  quote: "glm-5 8.33 97.92 37.50 100 72.80" and "glm-4p7 4.17 100 39.58 97.92 —"
  where: p.8, Table 2

- claim: Fix Rate separates models that tie on Resolved Rate.
  number: 4.65% vs 2.08% Fix at 2.08% Resolved; gpt-5.4 Fix 33.89 at 25.00 Resolved
  setup: OpenHands, gpt-4.1 vs gpt-oss-120b; Table 6 has all 18 models.
  quote: "bothgpt-4.1 and gpt-oss-120b resolve only2.08%ofSWE-EVO, but their Fix Rates are4.65%vs.2.08%"
  where: p.9; Table 6, p.22

- claim: Uncertainty is Wilson intervals over the 48 instances, not repeated runs.
  number: [14.9, 38.8] for 25.00%; one instance = 2.08 points
  setup: Single run per model-scaffold pair as far as the text shows; no seeds, repeats or run-to-run variance are mentioned anywhere.
  quote: "Representative 95% Wilson confidence intervals over task instances are [14.9, 38.8] for 25.00%, [10.2, 31.9] for 18.75%, [4.5, 22.2] for 10.42%, and [0.4, 10.9] for 2.08%"
  where: p.9

- claim: Failure analysis is an LLM judge (gpt-5-mini) assigning one primary label from a 7-category taxonomy to each unresolved SWE-agent trajectory, with no human validation.
  number: "over 60%" of gpt-5 failures are Instruction Following
  setup: SWE-agent only, 11 older models (not gpt-5.4, gpt-5.2, glm-5, kimi-k2p5). Categories: Syntax Error, Incorrect Implementation, Instruction Following, Tool-Use, Stuck in Loop, Gave Up Prematurely, Other.
  quote: "these labels are qualitative diagnostics rather than execution-based scores, and human agreement validation remains future work"
  where: p.10; Table 8, p.23

- claim: Tasks nobody solves bundle far more PRs than the easiest ones.
  number: 14.84 PRs vs 1.67; about 64% of instances are solved by no model-scaffold pair
  setup: Grouped by number of model-scaffold combinations resolving each instance.
  quote: "unresolved-by-all instances average 14.84 PRs, compared with 1.67 for the easiest group"
  where: pp.10-11

- claim: Dropping the PR/issue text lowers scores modestly.
  number: gpt-5: 14.58 / 16.67 (note only) vs 18.75 / 20.83
  setup: 10 models, OpenHands / SWE-agent, Table 4.
  quote: "gpt-5-08-0714.58 16.67 18.75 20.83"
  where: p.20

LIMITS
- Conceded: Python libraries only; 48 instances with 54.2% from dvc; limited statistical power; Fix Rate "weights tests equally and does not measure code quality, maintainability, or patch minimality"; the judge labels are unvalidated.
- Not shown: no repeated runs; no cost, token or wall-clock metrics (only average turns, in Figure 6b); no trajectory grading beyond the failure labels; no same-scaffold SWE-bench Verified comparison; no contamination analysis, though the repos are public and inherited from SWE-bench.
- Evaluation is on the final repository state only; a PR-by-PR variant is named as future work.
- Artifact release is stated as planned ("We plan to release"), though a GitHub URL is printed.

BUILDS ON: SWE-bench (Jimenez et al., 2024) for repos, environments and the Resolved Rate; SWE-gym (Pan et al., 2024) for the seed pool; SWE-agent (Yang et al., 2024a) for the scaffold and the failure-analysis method; OpenHands (Wang et al., 2024d).

CODE: none.

FIGURES: Figure 4, p.6: "SWE-EVO is markedly more demanding than SWE-Bench, with longer specifications, broader patch scope, and heavier test suites in both mean and max." Six paired bars (spec words 2390.5 vs 195.1, files 20.9 vs 1.7, F2P 81.4 vs 9.1, total tests 874.0 vs 120.8) show the scale gap at a glance.

PROBLEMS
- Words are run together throughout the extraction ("introduceSWE-EVO"); numbers are intact.
- Internal inconsistencies in the source: o3 on SWE-agent is 6.25 in Table 2 but 4.17 in Table 6. deepseek-v3p2 at 23.40 is not a multiple of 1/48 (it is 11/47). Text says "OpenAI (10 models)" but the tables list 9; the total is 18.
- Table 5 has Resolved above Fix for some repos (dvc on SWE-agent 8.72 vs 5.63), which the definition forbids; the per-repo values look like something other than per-repo rates. Do not cite Table 5.
- Table 7's "FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS rates" are never defined and several pairs sum to exactly 100 (65.68 + 34.32), so they are not independent pass rates. Do not cite as such.
- No embedded instructions aimed at the reader. Pages 24-30 hold task text only.
